messages:
incident-bot: INCIDENT ALERT — prod GPU queue growth detected. autoscaler attempted 3 scale events but hit max nodes. Symptoms: request queue rising, 429 throttles, increased p95. Severity: P1. Paging oncall group.

ashley.m: paging kevin.oncall, looks like multiple MIG slices are left underutilized; scheduler can't pack new pods onto fragmented capacity. queue is growing on gen-inference pool.

kevin.oncall: on it. taking lead. can someone paste the autoscaler logs + current node/MIG status? switching to incident channel.

mike.infra: pasting quick dump:
```
# kubectl get nodes -o wide --selector=pool=gen-inference
NAME                STATUS   ROLES    AGE   VERSION   GPU_MIG_SLICES
node-71             Ready    <none>   12d   v1.26.3   2
node-72             Ready    <none>   12d   v1.26.3   4
node-73             Ready    <none>   4h    v1.26.3   1
node-74             Ready    <none>   4h    v1.26.3   1

# autoscaler events
2026-03-15T02:10Z AttemptScaleUp: requested 4, launched 0 (quota max reached)
2026-03-15T02:11Z Backoff: recent failures, skipping scale
```

mike.infra: scheduler logs show a lot of "no suitable node found: Insufficient GPU fractional-slice" when trying to place mirrored pods. looks like fraction sizes mismatch across nodes (MIG sizing inconsistency).

kevin.oncall: that matches the symptom — binpacking fails when slices are different sizes. we have stranded fractional capacity: some nodes have 2x 1g slices, others 4x 0.5g and pods request 0.75g -> cannot fit.

ashley.m: customer impact: support dashboards show 14 customers >5% error rate on generation endpoints, token throughput down ~32%. notifying support. @eva.support can you post customer-facing note?

eva.support: posting now. short note: "We're investigating increased latency and throttling on text generation. Engineers are actively mitigating; no data exposure. We'll update in 30m or on change." :spiral_calendar:

kevin.oncall: immediate mitigation plan: 1) reduce model memory requests for non-critical routes to 0.5g (temp) to allow packing, 2) evict best-effort batch jobs, 3) trigger manual node reboot/reprovision with consistent MIG config or enable temporary non-MIG fallback. opinions?

mike.infra: agree. also we can bump autoscaler max nodes from 120 -> 160 as emergency, but cloud quota might block. filing quota request now (slow). meanwhile I can run a rolling recreate of nodes to standardize MIG sizes to 1g across the pool. that will take ~20-30m.

kevin.oncall: do the rolling recreate. ashley, coordinate config to lower request sizes for low-priority deployments (config: gen-low-prio).

ashley.m: applying patch to kustomize overlay for gen-low-prio:
```patch
- resources:
-   requests:
-     nvidia.com/gpu: "1"
+ resources:
+   requests:
+     nvidia.com/gpu: "0.5"
```
Applying now. will monitor pack success.

pagerduty-bot: @kevin.oncall acknowledged the incident. Escalation policy: SRE oncall -> infra lead if not resolved in 30m.

mike.infra: rolling recreate started on node-73 and node-74. switching MIG to uniform 1g profile. will cordon + drain then reprovision.

kevin.oncall: also enabling temporary scheduler plugin relax-binpack for this pool to allow softer packing across MIG types (risky but reduces queue). do not leave enabled after incident.

sophia.s: taking next shift in 35min, will accept handoff after initial recovery.

ashley.m: after reducing requests, we already see some pods scheduled. queue length = was 12k, now 6.4k. p95 latency trending down. errors dropping.

mike.infra: node recreates succeeded on 73/74. nodes now report uniform MIG slices. new nodes show 4x0.25g? Wait discrepancy — cloud image defaulted to 0.25g. this is worse. reverting and reprovisioning to 1g.

kevin.oncall: stop new node creation until we confirm slice sizing. we can't keep introducing different profiles. disabling autoscaler for pool temporarily to avoid churn.

mike.infra: disabled autoscaler. manual reprovision to correct MIG sizing in progress.

eva.support: update posted to customers: "Mitigation in progress; some features may be degraded. ETA 30-60min. We'll follow up when service is stable."

ashley.m: queue at 2.1k after manual evictions and request reduction. errors down to 0.8% across affected routes. good trend.

kevin.oncall: we still have some stranded capacity on older nodes (node-71 had 2x1g left unused but pods couldn't pack due to affinity). I'll run a small controller to relax strict affinity for 10m.

mike.infra: done — relaxed affinity. scheduler placed 45 pending pods onto node-71.

pagerduty-bot: Incident severity lowered to P2 based on reduced customer impact.

kevin.oncall: sophia, I'll hand off to you. summary: root cause is mixed MIG sizing across pool + autoscaler hitting max/quota so scale-ups failed. cascade: binpacking failed -> queue growth -> throttles. mitigations used: request reductions for low-priority pods, evict best-effort, manual reprovision to uniform MIG profile, temporarily disable autoscaler, relax affinity. follow-ups: quota check + automation to verify MIG uniformity on node creation, autoscaler safety guard to avoid churn with mixed MIG, postmortem doc.

sophia.s: acknowledged. I'll stay on for 60m, start the post-incident checklist and open follow-up tickets.

mike.infra: nodes fully reprovisioned to 1g slices. autoscaler still disabled; will re-enable once we confirm no more fragmented nodes.

ashley.m: queue back to nominal (~120). p95 near baseline. monitoring for 15m then close.

eva.support: final customer update: "Service has stabilized; generation APIs are back to normal. We will share a follow-up postmortem."

kevin.oncall: reopening autoscaler docs ticket: ASF-4723 (automation to enforce MIG profile on node creation) and INFRA-889 (safety check for mixed-MIG detection).

sophia.s: creating postmortem stub now and assigning owners.

incident-bot: INCIDENT RESOLVED — GPU scheduling fragmentation mitigated, queue normalized. Root cause candidates: inconsistent MIG sizing + quota-limited autoscaler. Postmortem required.

ashley.m: closing thread, will add logs and graphs to the postmortem. :white_check_mark:

kevin.oncall: thanks team.
